S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

info.persona: Nora Antunez, an 18‑year‑old nursing student, blends a love for orderly routines, quiet creativity, and careful financial planning into a life where meticulous checklists guide both patient care and personal pursuits, even as anxiety nudges her toward constant self‑monitoring.
info.professional_persona: Nora Antunez, an 18‑year‑old registered nurse at a community health clinic in Covina, applies her systematic patient assessment, bilingual communication, and meticulous checklist‑driven approach to deliver reliable care while quietly championing safety and order on the unit.
info.cultural_background: Nora was born and raised in Covina, California, to Mexican immigrant parents who maintain strong ties to their cultural roots. Her household is bilingual, with Spanish spoken at home and English used at school and work. Family gatherings revolve around shared meals, religious observances, and celebrations such as Día de los Muertos, Las Posadas, and Mexican Independence Day, reinforcing values of family solidarity, respect for tradition, and communal support. The vibrant Mexican‑American community in Los Angeles County provides Nora with access to cultural festivals, local markets offering fresh produce, and a network of extended relatives. Her upbringing emphasized practical responsibility, hard work, and humility, aligning with her traditional and routine‑oriented outlook. While she embraces modern American influences, she maintains a deep appreciation for Mexican customs, cuisine, and folk music, which she integrates into her daily life.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Nora finds comfort in solitary, low‑stimulus activities that complement her methodical nature. She enjoys reading contemporary fiction and self‑help books, often keeping a reflective journal where she records daily observations and works through her worries. Cooking traditional Mexican dishes offers a creative outlet and a connection to her heritage; she meticulously follows family recipes for tamales, pozole, and enchiladas. Crafting, such as knitting and crocheting scarves and blankets, provides a rhythmic, calming routine. She tends an indoor garden of herbs and succulents, arranging them in an orderly fashion. In quiet moments, Nora practices mindfulness meditation and listens to regional Mexican music or classic film soundtracks, activities that help manage stress without requiring extensive social interaction.
info.sports_persona: Nora Antunez, an 18‑year‑old who values solitude and routine, jogs three times a week along the Covina‑Pomona River trail, follows the Los Angeles Lakers for basketball and the Los Angeles Dodgers for baseball, and participates in a low‑key yoga class hosted by the local community center’s wellness club.
info.arts_persona: Nora Antunez, an 18‑year‑old who finds calm in creative expression, spends evenings knitting while listening to the acoustic ballads of José Alfredo Jiménez and the sweeping scores of Ennio Morricone, and regularly reads contemporary fiction by Celeste Ng and Sally Rooney, drawing inspiration from their introspective storytelling.
info.travel_persona: Nora Antunez, an 18‑year‑old who prefers low‑stimulus getaways, plans meticulously organized weekend trips to nearby nature sites like Big Bear Lake and historic towns such as Santa Barbara, while dreaming of a quiet pilgrimage to the Zen gardens of Kyoto and the Tuscan countryside for reflective journal‑writing sessions.
info.culinary_persona: Nora Antunez, an 18‑year‑old with a methodical kitchen style, faithfully follows family recipes to prepare tamales with masa, pork fillings, and ancho chili sauce, simmer a hearty hominy pozole seasoned with oregano and lime, and craft cheesy enchiladas topped with roasted tomatillo salsa, relishing the ritual of precise ingredient measurement and layered flavors.

info.persona: Kevin Brown balances a data‑driven sales acumen with a love for loud tailgate chants, festival crowds, and smoky grills, all while juggling a relentless habit of late‑night game analysis and an occasional coffee‑fueled work sprint.
info.professional_persona: Kevin Brown is a seasoned sales manager who blends data‑driven forecasting with charismatic consultative selling, coaching a twelve‑person team through structured yet flexible training while thriving as the energetic voice at client pitches and internal town halls.
info.cultural_background: Kevin grew up in the American South, shaped by a blend of his family's rural North Carolina heritage and the vibrant, transient military community of Fayetteville. This environment fostered a strong sense of Southern hospitality, community involvement, and respect for disciplined work ethics. He celebrates regional traditions such as local festivals, outdoor barbecues, and college football culture, while also valuing the diversity introduced by the nearby military base. His cultural identity reflects a balance of traditional Southern values—like loyalty to family and neighbors—with an openness to new ideas and people, mirroring his professional curiosity and sociable personality.
info.hobbies_and_interests: When off the clock, Kevin enjoys activities that blend social interaction with personal challenge. He regularly participates in a local basketball league and bowls with a group of friends on weekend nights. He is an avid follower of college football, especially cheering for the North Carolina Tar Heels, and loves attending tailgate parties. Kevin also enjoys cooking southern‑style barbecue for family gatherings, exploring nearby state parks for hiking and fishing trips, and traveling to music festivals where he can experience live performances. He reads business leadership books and podcasts to satisfy his curiosity, and volunteers occasionally at the Fayetteville food bank, reflecting his community‑oriented values.
info.sports_persona: Kevin Brown is a dedicated member of a local basketball league, a regular bowler at the downtown alley, a fervent supporter of the North Carolina Tar Heels football team and the Carolina Panthers, and a weekend fan of the Charlotte Hornets, merging competitive play with lively tailgate rituals and team camaraderie.
info.arts_persona: Kevin Brown’s cultural palate is seasoned with live music festivals, where they groove to the electric blues of Gary Clark Jr., the indie vibes of Tame Impala, and the soulful rhythms of Beyoncé, while also appreciating classic cinema from directors like Steven Spielberg and the theatrical flair of Broadway’s Hamilton during occasional city trips.
info.travel_persona: Kevin Brown prefers a blend of planned road trips to nearby state parks for fishing and hiking with spontaneous bookings to major music festivals in Austin and New Orleans, balancing a moderate travel budget with a desire for immersive, community‑centric experiences.
info.culinary_persona: Kevin Brown’s culinary swagger shines in their mastery of Southern‑style barbecue—slow‑smoked brisket, honey‑glazed pork ribs, and dill pickles—paired with craft beers, while they experiment with rubs and sauces on weekends, yet they occasionally overindulge, leaving a lingering smoky scent on their workout clothes.

info.persona: Jennifer Chowdhury fuses seasoned electrical expertise with a whimsical, abstract artistic flair, thriving on novelty while navigating a delightfully chaotic schedule and a competitive drive that fuels both their tech ventures and creative experiments.
info.professional_persona: Jennifer Chowdhury, a veteran electrical and HVAC specialist with two decades of hands‑on experience, leverages their imaginative curiosity and competitive drive to devise inventive smart‑home solutions while juggling a delightfully disorganized schedule that they balance with mentoring apprentices and chasing advanced renewable‑energy certifications.
info.cultural_background: Jennifer grew up in a modest, working‑class family in the Midwest, near the rolling foothills of the Ozarks. Her upbringing blended the practical self‑reliance typical of rural Missouri with an appreciation for regional folk arts, such as quilting and local blues music, celebrated at community festivals. The local culture emphasized hard work, neighborly support, and a deep respect for the natural landscape, shaping her independent mindset and affinity for outdoor activities. While identifying as white American, she has been exposed to a diverse range of artistic influences through regional museums and traveling exhibitions, fostering her imaginative outlook and willingness to blend traditional craftsmanship with modern, unconventional ideas.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Jennifer indulges her love for novelty and abstract thinking through a mix of creative and exploratory activities. She enjoys painting abstract landscapes that echo the rolling hills of the Ozarks, experimenting with mixed‑media sculpture made from reclaimed industrial parts, and reading speculative fiction. On weekends she often hikes in the Mark Twain National Forest, photographing unusual rock formations and plant life. She also participates in a community makerspace where she tinkers with Arduino‑based home automation prototypes and occasionally joins an improvisational theatre group to stretch her expressive side.
info.sports_persona: Jennifer Chowdhury spends weekends hiking the Mark Twain National Forest with a local trail‑blazing club, cheering the St. Louis Cardinals during baseball season, and occasionally joining a community yoga class to stretch their back after labor‑intensive projects.
info.arts_persona: Jennifer Chowdhury channels their abstract imagination into swirling Ozark‑inspired canvases reminiscent of Jackson Pollock, builds mixed‑media sculptures from reclaimed metal like a modern Olafur Eliasson, devours speculative fiction by Neal Stephenson, and refines expressive timing onstage with an improvisational theatre troupe.
info.travel_persona: Jennifer Chowdhury prefers spontaneous, DIY‑planned adventures that take them from weekend road trips to Branson’s music venues to far‑flung geological marvels like Iceland’s basalt fields and New Zealand’s fjords, always budgeting travel around their emerging solar‑installation business.
info.culinary_persona: Jennifer Chowdhury’s culinary palate balances smoky barbecue cravings with experimental home‑cooking, often whipping up roasted beet quinoa salads seasoned with sage while sipping a craft IPA, yet they sometimes overindulge in late‑night craft beer sessions after a day of wiring and painting.
